methodologyNotes: Specs sourced from Newegg product search pages (newegg.com, accessed June 2026), Laptop Mag best-portable-monitors roundup (laptopmag.com/best-picks/best-portable-monitors, June 2026), XDA Developers best portable monitors roundup (xda-developers.com/best-portable-monitors, June 2026), and Newegg espresso Displays category pages. Manufacturer pages for ASUS (asus.com), ROG (rog.asus.com), espresso (espressodisplays.com via Newegg listings), and UPERFECT were attempted but many returned 403/404 or geo-redirected to non-US pages — Newegg and Laptop Mag are used as primary authoritative fallbacks where manufacturer pages were inaccessible. priceUsd is US MSRP or primary US retail asking price for the base/standard config as found at time of access; null when no USD price was recoverable. Numbers are stored unit-free; units implied by specKey names (size_in = diagonal inches, refresh_hz = Hz, weight_lb = pounds). ports is a concise string of video and primary power-delivery ports. touchscreen is boolean. release is YYYY-MM or YYYY. Specs marked null were genuinely unknown from recoverable sources — no guessing. accessedAt is 2026-06-15 on all sources. Products selected to represent the full buyer-comparison landscape in 2026: budget IPS, mid-range IPS, gaming high-refresh, OLED, professional touch, ultra-premium 4K touch, and compact 14-inch tiers.
